ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in the Middle East changed by +0.334 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.247 to +0.422), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.824 °C.

cautions: The confidence interval is wide compared with the trend, so the size of the change is uncertain.
ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in the Middle East changed by −0.0065 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.0127 to −0.0002), which is statistically significant (p = 0.04). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is a decrease of about 0.0161 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water in the topsoil
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water in the topsoil in the Middle East shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.14): the estimate is −0.16 kg/m² per decade (95% confidence interval −0.37 to +0.05). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in the Middle East shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.41): the estimate is −0.029 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.098 to +0.040). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in the Middle East shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.91): the estimate is +0.001 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.014 to +0.014). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
